output.title: Glasshouse inquiry
output.problem: A lamp accompanies the opening of a fictional seedling’s leaves. Do leaves follow light itself, immediate warmth, or warmth that persists after the light? Construct an inquiry that can distinguish the three explicit explanations. There is no hidden correct answer.
output.goal: Make one result/study whose prediction groups each contain only one explanation. Short solutions are welcome. You need not tour all controls, find a secret answer, or take a minimum number of actions.

laws.problem: A lamp accompanies the opening of a fictional seedling’s leaves. Do leaves follow light itself, immediate warmth, or warmth that persists after the light? Construct an inquiry that can distinguish the three explicit explanations. There is no hidden correct answer.
laws.trial: A method compares two chambers over three moments; warmth before the first controlled moment is zero. The reference chamber stays dark. The test chamber is steadily lit or receives a middle-moment pulse. Record leaf opening reads all three moments. Automatic moments are forecasts, not player turns.
laws.controls: A method + a control makes a new reusable method. Cool/warm replaces the thermostat setting in the child; release removes it. Pulse/steady changes the lamp schedule. Parents remain unchanged. A clamp overrides retained heat too: cooling changes the causal question rather than automatically improving every method.
laws.observe: A method + Record leaf opening produces a forecast-result object. All explanations and exact trajectories are already inspectable. Recording commits your selected method as an operand; it does not reveal a secret measurement.
laws.study: Two results combine into a study retaining their methods. It groups explanations that predict identical opening diaries across those methods. Combining a result with itself adds nothing. Signature notation: 0 means closed, 1 open; dark-chamber diary / test-chamber diary; | separates methods.
laws.goal: Make one result/study whose prediction groups each contain only one explanation. Short solutions are welcome. You need not tour all controls, find a secret answer, or take a minimum number of actions.
laws.disclosure: inspect shows full per-moment light, warmth and opening forecasts; offers shows every legal pair and exact output, including duplicates. Inputs are inexhaustible. There are no inventories, budgets, scores or hidden recipes.
laws.limits: These deterministic leaf-opening laws are invented, not real botany or a historical account. Identifiability under toy models does not prove a real causal explanation.

models.label: Leaves follow light directly
models.law: Leaves open exactly when the lamp is on. Warmth does not affect opening; uncontrolled chamber warmth follows the current lamp.

models.label: Leaves follow immediate warmth
models.law: An uncontrolled chamber is warm exactly when the lamp is on. Leaves open exactly when warm.

models.label: Leaves follow retained warmth
models.law: An uncontrolled chamber stays warm while the lamp is on OR was on in the previous moment. Leaves open exactly when warm.

recorded.experience: Clear, compact causal-identifiability puzzle. I understood the needed pair of interventions from the initial laws, checked two previews, then built the joint study in five combinations. It felt more like expressing a solution in an interface than discovering one.
recorded.worthDoing: Choosing complementary experiments was worthwhile: free warmth after a pulse separates retained heat, while cooling under steady light separates direct light from either heat account. Seeing the joint prediction groups made the logical distinction concrete.
recorded.keep: Keep explicit competing laws, exact previews, immutable reusable methods, and the honest statement that no secret measurement or correct explanation is being revealed.
recorded.shortenRemoveChange: Shorten repeated forecast formatting into a compact comparison table. Consider allowing a selected method to enter a study directly, since observing merely materializes already known forecasts; the two observation moves were administrative. Keep the short completion path rather than requiring a tour of redundant controls.
recorded.stoppedBecause: The two-method study has three singleton prediction groups and the public goal is satisfied. More branches would not improve this solution.
